# The Steel-Structure Foundation & Anchor Bolt Field Guide

> A 62-page field guide by Hicham Zein Eddine (20+ years on steel-structure and foundation sites in Qatar, the UAE, Poland and Canada) on setting anchor bolts for steel structures right the first time, from drawing review to grouted base plate. Price: CAD$30 on Gumroad: https://canadacorp.gumroad.com/l/anchor-bolt-guide
Kindle edition on Amazon (ASIN B0HD6LLW8G): https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HD6LLW8G

Applies to pre-engineered buildings (PEB), hot-rolled steel frames, warehouses, transmission towers and poles, telecom masts and monopoles, car-park shades and canopies.

## Free articles

- [How to make and use an anchor bolt template](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/anchor-bolt-template/): Why every anchor bolt group needs a template, how to fabricate it to match the column base plate, and why you should keep it to drill the base plates.
- [ASTM F1554 Grade 36 vs 55 vs 105: which anchor bolt grade?](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/astm-f1554-grades/): The three ASTM F1554 anchor bolt grades, their yield strengths and typical uses, how they relate to ISO 8.8 and 10.9, and why you must measure the diameter yourself.
- [Anchor bolt setting tolerances: what is acceptable?](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/anchor-bolt-tolerances/): Typical anchor bolt tolerances for bolt group position, spacing, projection and top elevation, based on AISC and ACI 117 practice, and what to do when bolts fall outside them.
- [Misaligned anchor bolts after casting: the correct fixes](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/misaligned-anchor-bolts/): What to do when the bolt group does not line up with the base plate holes: under 6 mm, 6 to 12 mm, and over 12 mm. Why you should never bend anchor bolts.
- [L-bolt and J-bolt hooks: which way should they face?](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/l-bolt-j-bolt-hook-orientation/): Hooked anchor bolts must face the outside of the foundation. Plus the two-nuts-two-washers rule, embedment depth, and the tie-check-weld sequence.
- [Pre-pour checklist for anchor bolts and foundations (final gate)](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/pre-pour-checklist/): The final gate before casting a steel-structure foundation: bolts, formwork, rebar, spacers, cleaning, threads, access, lighting, vibrator and the inspector's signature.
- [Pouring concrete around anchor bolts without moving them](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/pouring-concrete-around-anchor-bolts/): Never aim the pump at the bolts, pour all ready foundations at once to avoid cold joints, and stop only at a designed construction joint.
- [Base plate grouting: why it must be non-shrink grout](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/base-plate-non-shrink-grout/): How the base plate sits on levelling nuts, why the gap must be filled with non-shrink grout (ASTM C1107), and how to fix grout voids under the plate.
- [Protecting and repairing anchor bolt threads](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/damaged-anchor-bolt-threads/): Tape the threads before casting, and how to fix concrete-coated, impact-damaged or severely damaged anchor bolt threads.
- [SRC vs OPC: which cement for foundations?](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/src-vs-opc-cement-foundations/): Sulfate-Resisting Cement below ground, Ordinary Portland Cement above ground, with typical grades for blinding, footings, tie beams and column necks.
- [Your first site as a new engineer: earning the crew's respect](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/first-day-on-site-new-engineer/): For engineering students and new graduates: how to work with tradesmen who have more years on site, avoid approval traps, and protect your word.
- [Anchor bolt embedment depth: how deep should anchor bolts go?](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/anchor-bolt-embedment-depth/): Embedment depth is a design value, not a site estimate. The common 10 x diameter rule of thumb, what governs the real figure (ACI 318 Ch. 17, EN 1992-4) and how to hold it during the pour.
- [Levelling nuts or shims under a column base plate?](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/base-plate-levelling-nuts-shims/): Why the base plate sits above the concrete on levelling nuts or shims, how the gap is used to level and plumb the column, the tolerances to check, and why the gap is then filled with non-shrink grout.
- [Post-installed anchors: chemical vs mechanical vs undercut](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/post-installed-anchors-chemical-vs-mechanical/): When you need drilled-in anchors instead of cast-in bolts, how chemical, expansion and undercut anchors work, the standards behind them, and the installation rules that prevent failures.
- [Steel structure foundation sequence: from drawing to grouted base plate](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/steel-structure-foundation-sequence/): The site sequence for PEB, warehouse, tower and canopy foundations in 15 steps: drawings, survey, access, excavation, blinding, formwork, rebar, anchor bolts, base plate, grout, QA/QC and fixes.
- [Anchor bolts for poles, towers and canopies under uplift](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/articles/pole-tower-anchor-bolts-uplift/): Telecom masts, transmission towers, lighting poles and open canopies put anchor bolts in tension. What changes on site: embedment, hook orientation, grout and tolerances.

- [Pre-pour checklist (final gate)](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/checklist/): printable, no sign-up.
- [About the author](https://canadaservcorp-tech.github.io/anchors-book-/about/): Hicham Zein Eddine's site experience, topics, and workshops on anchor bolts, foundations and steel erection.

## Book contents

15 chapters: drawings, setting out, safe access, excavation, trench bottom, anti-termite treatment, polyethylene sheet, blinding, footing formwork, rebar, anchor bolts, base plate and grouting, post-installed anchors, QA/QC, troubleshooting; appendices on anchor-bolt specifications, concrete testing, inspection checklist and unit conversions.

## Note

This content is provided for professional educational use and does not replace a licensed structural engineer or the governing code for your jurisdiction. Always verify against the approved documents for your project.
